subject: math
cluster: Use functions to model relationships between quantities
intro: These problems require a full qualitative analysis of a function's graph. Reason about several features at once (increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear, and relative rate of change), translate carefully between graphs and real-world stories, and explain when a graph does NOT match a description. Watch for subtle distinctions such as constant versus slowly increasing, and growth that speeds up (concave up) versus growth that slows down (concave down).

items.prompt: A graph of height versus time has four segments in order: from $x=0$ to $x=2$ it rises as a straight line; from $x=2$ to $x=4$ it rises as a curve that gets steeper; from $x=4$ to $x=6$ it is horizontal; from $x=6$ to $x=8$ it falls as a straight line. Describe each segment using both increasing/decreasing/constant AND linear/nonlinear.
items.answer: From $x=0$ to $x=2$: increasing and linear. From $x=2$ to $x=4$: increasing and nonlinear. From $x=4$ to $x=6$: constant (and linear). From $x=6$ to $x=8$: decreasing and linear.

steps: Segment 1 ($x=0$ to $x=2$): the graph goes up, so increasing; it is a straight line, so linear.
Segment 2 ($x=2$ to $x=4$): the graph goes up, so increasing; it is a curve whose steepness changes, so the rate of change is not constant, making it nonlinear.
Segment 3 ($x=4$ to $x=6$): the graph is horizontal, so the value does not change, making it constant. A horizontal segment is a straight line, so it is also linear.
Segment 4 ($x=6$ to $x=8$): the graph goes down, so decreasing; it is a straight line, so linear.
solution.answer: Increasing/linear, then increasing/nonlinear, then constant, then decreasing/linear.

items.prompt: A car's distance from a toll booth is graphed against time. The graph rises steeply as a straight line, then rises as a curve that flattens out (still going up but more slowly), then becomes horizontal, then falls steeply to zero as a straight line. Tell the story of the car's trip, naming what happens in each of the four phases.
items.answer: The car drives away from the toll booth at a fast, steady speed (steep straight rise); then it keeps moving away but slows down (rising curve that flattens); then it stops, staying the same distance away (horizontal); then it returns quickly to the toll booth (steep straight fall to zero).

steps: Phase 1, steep straight rise: distance increases at a constant fast rate, so the car moves away from the booth quickly and steadily.
Phase 2, rising curve that flattens: distance is still increasing so the car keeps moving away, but the flattening means the rate is decreasing, so the car is slowing down.
Phase 3, horizontal: distance does not change, so the car is stopped (it stays the same distance from the booth, it does not return).
Phase 4, steep straight fall to zero: distance decreases quickly back to $0$, so the car drives quickly back to the toll booth.
solution.answer: Drives away fast and steadily, keeps going but slows down, stops, then returns quickly to the booth.

items.prompt: Sketch a graph of $y$ versus $x$ that does ALL of the following in order: (1) increases nonlinearly so that it grows faster and faster, (2) increases linearly, (3) stays constant, (4) decreases nonlinearly so that it falls more and more slowly. Describe in words the shape your sketch should have for each of the four parts.
items.answer: Part 1: an upward curve that bends upward (concave up), getting steeper. Part 2: a straight slanted segment going up. Part 3: a horizontal segment. Part 4: a downward curve that starts steep and flattens as it falls (concave up while decreasing), so it drops more and more slowly.

steps: Part 1, increases faster and faster: draw a rising curve that gets steeper as you move right (concave up).
Part 2, increases linearly: continue with a straight slanted line segment that rises at a constant slope.
Part 3, stays constant: draw a horizontal segment at the height where part 2 ended.
Part 4, decreases more and more slowly: draw a falling curve that starts steep and gradually flattens toward horizontal, so each later bit drops less than the bit before.
solution.answer: Concave-up rising curve, then straight rising segment, then horizontal segment, then a falling curve that flattens as it goes down.

items.prompt: Two students each describe the same situation. Mia says: 'The temperature rose steadily all morning.' Leo says: 'The temperature rose, but it warmed up faster and faster as the morning went on.' The graph of temperature versus time is a single smooth curve that bends upward and gets steeper. Whose description matches the graph, and explain why the other description is wrong.
items.answer: Leo's description matches. The curve gets steeper, so the rate of increase is growing, meaning the temperature warms faster and faster. Mia is wrong because 'rose steadily' means a constant rate, which would be a straight line, not a curve that steepens.

steps: The graph is always going up, so the temperature is increasing for both descriptions.
The curve gets steeper as time passes, so the rate of change is increasing, not constant.
Leo says it warmed faster and faster, which matches an increasing rate (a steepening curve).
Mia says it rose steadily, which means a constant rate of change. A constant rate would be a straight line, not a steepening curve, so Mia's description does not match.
solution.answer: Leo matches; Mia is wrong because 'steadily' means a constant rate (a straight line), not a steepening curve.

items.prompt: A graph of water level in a tank versus time rises, then is horizontal, then rises again. The first rising part is a curve that starts steep and flattens as it climbs, and the second rising part is a straight line that is less steep than the initial steepness of the first part (but still rising). Order the three intervals from fastest filling at the start of the interval to slowest, and state which interval is not filling at all.
items.answer: Fastest start to slowest start: the first interval, then the third interval, then the horizontal middle interval. The first curve begins steepest (it starts steep then flattens), the third straight segment is less steep so it fills more slowly, and the horizontal middle interval is not filling at all (rate $0$).

steps: Interval 1 is a curve that starts steep and then flattens, so at its very start the level is rising fastest.
Interval 3 is a straight rising line whose slope is given to be less steep than interval 1's initial steepness, so it fills at a steady positive rate that is slower than interval 1's start.
Interval 2 (the horizontal segment) has the level unchanged, so the tank is not filling at all there; its rate is $0$.
Ranking the starting rates from fastest to slowest: interval 1 (steep curve start) is greater than interval 3 (steady, less-steep rise), which is greater than interval 2 (horizontal, rate $0$).
The middle interval (horizontal) is the one not filling at all.
solution.answer: Fastest to slowest start: interval 1, then interval 3, then the horizontal middle interval, which is not filling.

items.prompt: Describe the graph below completely in words, covering increasing/decreasing/constant AND linear/nonlinear for every piece. The graph of $y$ versus $x$: from $x=0$ to $x=3$ it falls as a straight line; from $x=3$ to $x=5$ it is horizontal; from $x=5$ to $x=9$ it rises as a curve that gets less and less steep; from $x=9$ to $x=11$ it rises as a straight line.
items.answer: From $x=0$ to $x=3$: decreasing and linear. From $x=3$ to $x=5$: constant. From $x=5$ to $x=9$: increasing and nonlinear (the curve flattens, so the rate of increase is slowing). From $x=9$ to $x=11$: increasing and linear.

steps: $x=0$ to $x=3$: the line goes down and is straight, so decreasing and linear.
$x=3$ to $x=5$: the graph is horizontal, so the value is constant.
$x=5$ to $x=9$: the graph goes up so it is increasing; it is a curve whose steepness changes, so it is nonlinear, and since it gets less steep the rate of increase is slowing.
$x=9$ to $x=11$: the graph goes up and is straight, so increasing and linear.
solution.answer: Decreasing/linear, then constant, then increasing/nonlinear (slowing), then increasing/linear.

items.prompt: A skydiver's height above the ground is graphed against time. The graph starts high, falls as a curve that gets steeper, then falls as a straight line, then falls as a curve that flattens out, then becomes horizontal at height $0$. Match each of these phrases to the correct phase: (a) free fall speeding up, (b) falling at a steady speed, (c) slowing down before landing, (d) on the ground. Then say whether the steady-speed phase is linear or nonlinear.
items.answer: (a) free fall speeding up = the first curve that gets steeper. (b) falling at a steady speed = the straight falling segment. (c) slowing down before landing = the curve that flattens out. (d) on the ground = the horizontal segment at height $0$. The steady-speed phase is linear.

steps: Curve that gets steeper while falling: the downward rate is increasing, so the diver is speeding up, matching (a) free fall speeding up.
Straight falling segment: a constant negative rate means a steady speed, matching (b).
Curve that flattens while falling: the downward rate is decreasing, so the diver is slowing, matching (c).
Horizontal segment at height $0$: no change in height at the ground, matching (d) on the ground.
A straight segment has a constant rate of change, so the steady-speed phase is linear.
solution.answer: a = steepening curve, b = straight fall, c = flattening curve, d = horizontal at $0$; steady-speed phase is linear.

items.prompt: A student claims that the following graph shows a population that 'grew quickly, then grew slowly, then shrank.' The graph rises as a curve that gets less steep, then rises as a steeper straight line, then is horizontal. Explain why the student's description does NOT match the graph, and give a correct description.
items.answer: It does not match. The first curve flattens, so the population grows quickly then slowly there, which fits the start. But the second part is a steeper straight rise, meaning growth speeds up again (not slows), and the last part is horizontal, meaning the population stays the same (not shrinks). A correct description: grew quickly then slowly, then grew faster again at a steady rate, then stayed constant.

steps: First part, rising curve that gets less steep: increasing with a slowing rate, so 'grew quickly then slowly' fits this piece only.
Second part, steeper straight rise: this is increasing at a faster steady rate, so growth speeds up again, contradicting 'then grew slowly' as the overall trend.
Third part, horizontal: the value is constant, so the population stays the same; it does not shrink, which would require a falling segment.
Because the graph never goes down, 'then shrank' is false, and the middle is faster growth, not slower.
Correct description: grows quickly then slows (curve flattening), then grows faster at a steady rate (steeper straight line), then stays constant (horizontal).
solution.answer: Wrong because the graph never falls (so it never shrinks) and the middle is faster steady growth; correctly it grows fast then slow, then faster steadily, then constant.

items.prompt: Two rising graphs of savings versus time are compared. Graph P is a straight line. Graph Q is a curve that bends upward and steepens. They start at the same point and end at the same point at the same time. Over the whole interval, which graph represents money that is increasing faster at the END of the interval, and which represents the larger average rate over the whole interval? Explain.
items.answer: At the end, Graph Q is increasing faster, because its upward bend makes it steepest near the end. Over the whole interval the average rate is the same for both, because they start and end at the same points over the same time, so they have equal total change and equal average rate of change.

steps: Average rate of change over the interval is total change in $y$ divided by total change in $x$. Both graphs share the same start and end points and the same time span.
Equal total $y$-change over equal time means both have the same average rate of change over the whole interval.
Graph Q bends upward and steepens, so its slope is small at the start and large at the end; Graph P has a constant slope equal to that shared average.
Therefore at the end Q is steeper than P, so Q is increasing faster at the end.
solution.answer: Q increases faster at the end; both have the same average rate over the whole interval.

items.prompt: Sketch a graph of distance from home versus time for this trip, and describe each piece: A person leaves home and walks at a steady pace to a park, rests at the park, then jogs home faster than they walked but at a steady pace. Tell how many segments your graph has, the direction and straightness of each, and which segment is steepest.
items.answer: Three segments. (1) A straight slanted line rising from $0$ (walking away at a steady pace). (2) A horizontal segment (resting at the park, distance unchanged). (3) A straight slanted line falling back to $0$ (jogging home steadily). The last segment is steepest because jogging is faster than walking, so distance changes more per unit time.

steps: Walking to the park at a steady pace: distance increases at a constant rate, so a straight rising line from $0$.
Resting at the park: distance from home does not change, so a horizontal segment.
Jogging home at a steady pace: distance decreases back to $0$ at a constant rate, so a straight falling line ending at $0$.
Jogging is faster than walking, so the falling segment covers distance more quickly per unit time, making it steeper than the rising segment.
The graph has three segments: rising straight, horizontal, falling straight, with the falling segment steepest.
solution.answer: Three segments: straight rise (walk), horizontal (rest), straight fall to $0$ (jog); the jog (last) segment is steepest.

items.prompt: A graph of a function has these features in order: increasing nonlinearly with growth that slows down, then constant, then decreasing linearly, then decreasing nonlinearly with the fall speeding up. For each of the four pieces, state whether the piece is concave (curving) or straight, and whether the value is going up, staying the same, or going down.
items.answer: Piece 1: curving (concave down), going up. Piece 2: straight, staying the same. Piece 3: straight, going down. Piece 4: curving (concave down), going down.

steps: Piece 1, increasing with growth slowing: the value goes up, and a slowing increase makes a curve that flattens, so it is curving (not straight).
Piece 2, constant: the value stays the same, shown by a horizontal straight segment.
Piece 3, decreasing linearly: the value goes down at a constant rate, so it is a straight falling line.
Piece 4, decreasing with the fall speeding up: the value goes down and the downward rate grows, so it is a curving (steepening downward) segment.

items.prompt: A cup of hot cocoa cools over time. Its temperature is graphed against time and falls as a curve that gets less and less steep, leveling off toward room temperature but never quite becoming horizontal during the graph. Explain why this graph is decreasing and nonlinear, and explain why describing the cooling as 'the cocoa cools at a steady rate' would be incorrect.
items.answer: The graph is decreasing because the temperature goes down the whole time. It is nonlinear because it is a curve whose steepness changes (it gets less steep), so the rate of change is not constant. 'Cools at a steady rate' would be wrong because a steady rate means a constant rate of change, which is a straight line; here the cooling slows down over time, so the rate is changing.

steps: The temperature falls throughout, so the function is decreasing.
The graph is a curve whose steepness decreases (it flattens), so the rate of change is not the same everywhere, which means it is nonlinear.
A steady rate of cooling would mean the temperature drops the same amount each minute, producing a straight line.
Since the curve flattens, the cocoa loses temperature faster at first and more slowly later, so the rate is not steady and the 'steady rate' description is incorrect.
solution.answer: Decreasing because temperature always falls; nonlinear because the curve flattens (changing rate); 'steady rate' is wrong since a steady rate is a straight line and the cooling actually slows.

items.prompt: A graph of a bicyclist's speed versus time (not distance) has these parts: rises as a straight line, stays horizontal, falls as a curve that flattens out near the bottom, then stays horizontal at a low value above $0$. Translate this into a story about the bicyclist's speed, and state during which part the speed is constant but not zero.
items.answer: The cyclist speeds up at a steady rate (straight rise), then holds a constant fast speed (first horizontal part), then slows down, braking hard at first and more gently as they slow (falling curve that flattens), then holds a constant slow speed (final horizontal part). The speed is constant but not zero during both horizontal parts, including the final low horizontal part above $0$.

steps: Straight rise in speed: speed increases at a constant rate, so the cyclist accelerates steadily.
First horizontal part: speed is constant, so the cyclist holds a steady fast speed.
Falling curve that flattens: speed decreases, and the flattening means the decrease slows, so the cyclist brakes hard at first then eases off.
Final horizontal part above $0$: speed is constant at a low value, so the cyclist rides steadily but slowly (still moving since the value is above $0$).
Both horizontal parts show constant speed; the final one is the constant, low, nonzero speed asked about.
solution.answer: Accelerates steadily, holds a fast speed, brakes (hard then gently), then holds a slow steady speed; constant-but-not-zero speed occurs on both horizontal parts, especially the final low one.

items.prompt: Compare two graphs of plant height versus time, both increasing the whole time. Graph M is concave up (bends upward, growth speeding up). Graph N is concave down (bends downward, growth slowing). For the same time interval, write which plant is growing faster at the START of the interval and which is growing faster at the END, assuming both start and end at the same heights at the same times.
items.answer: At the START, Graph N is growing faster (a concave-down curve is steepest near the beginning). At the END, Graph M is growing faster (a concave-up curve is steepest near the end). Both have the same average growth rate over the interval since they share start and end points.

steps: Concave up (M): slope starts small and increases, so M is least steep at the start and most steep at the end.
Concave down (N): slope starts large and decreases, so N is most steep at the start and least steep at the end.
At the start, N is steeper than M, so plant N grows faster at the start.
At the end, M is steeper than N, so plant M grows faster at the end.
Because both share the same start and end points over the same time, their average rates of change over the whole interval are equal.
solution.answer: N grows faster at the start, M grows faster at the end; equal average growth over the whole interval.

items.prompt: Four graphs of account balance versus time are described. Which one matches this story: 'The balance grew slowly at first, then grew faster and faster, then suddenly stayed the same'? (a) a straight rising line, then horizontal. (b) a curve that rises and gets steeper, then horizontal. (c) a curve that rises and flattens, then horizontal. (d) a straight rising line, then a straight falling line. Choose the matching graph and explain why each of the other three fails.
items.answer: Graph (b) matches. It rises with increasing steepness (grew faster and faster) then becomes horizontal (stayed the same). (a) fails because a straight line grows at a steady rate, not faster and faster. (c) fails because a flattening curve grows slower and slower, the opposite of faster and faster. (d) fails because its last part falls, meaning the balance decreases instead of staying the same.

steps: 'Grew faster and faster' means an increasing rate of change, which is a rising curve that gets steeper (concave up).
'Then suddenly stayed the same' means a horizontal segment after the rise.
Graph (b) has a steepening rise then a horizontal part, matching both features.
Graph (a) rises as a straight line, so the rate is steady, not faster and faster; it fails the 'faster and faster' part.
Graph (c) rises but flattens, so growth slows down, the opposite of faster and faster; it fails.
Graph (d) ends with a falling line, so the balance decreases rather than staying the same; it fails.
solution.answer: (b); (a) grows steadily not faster and faster, (c) slows down, (d) falls instead of staying the same.
